title: Introduce CI glue components and stabilize toolcache behavior for presubmit
author: Nina Rodriguez
description: Motivation: presubmit setup time variability and flaky toolcache misses have been a recurring source of slow feedback and transient CI failures. This change introduces a small 'CI glue' layer (shell + tiny Go helper) that normalizes toolcache keying across runners, implements a conservative cache warming step, and provides a stable fallback path for environment bootstrapping. Highlights: (1) toolcache stabilizer: canonicalizes cache keys by tool+version+os+arch+hash(manifest) to reduce redundant installs and cross-runner cache churn; (2) lightweight presubmit bootstrapper: a minimal wrapper that fast-paths common dev/lint installs and falls back to full bootstrap only when needed; (3) split lint plugins: move language-specific lint plugin bootstraps into isolated plugin manifests so CI can skip unrelated language installs for most PRs; (4) pinned build images: bump and pin a handful of base images (golang 1.21.8, node 20.15.1, python 3.11.6) to reduce indeterminism; (5) dep realignment: update our internal dep-hint index and devdeps to match the new toolcache keys and pinned images. The end-to-end effect in internal perf tests: median presubmit setup time reduced ~28% on changed-only runs and median cache miss rate fell from ~12% to ~3%. Rollout plan: staged rollout via opt-in feature-flag for CI lanes for one week, monitor presubmit latency and cache hit telemetry, then flip default. Post-merge remediation: rollback hook and key-prefix toggle added to allow immediate revert of toolcache keying if cross-region cache incompatibilities are observed. Checklist: - Implement CI glue helper and wrapper script - Add plugin manifests and split lint bootstraps - Bump and pin base images referenced in buildmanifests - Update CI job definitions to use new wrapper and cache key scheme - Add telemetry events for cache hits/misses and bootstrap fallback path - Add unit tests for key canonicalization - Validate in canary CI lane and then opt-in lanes - Document new plugin manifest format and keying in docs/ci/toolcache.md Testing done: small unit tests for canonicalization, integration runs in ephemeral CI with seeded cache, canary runs on long-lived branch for 48 hours, manual verification of lint paths for python/js/go. Links: internal dep index (link internal), Linear tickets ENG-2410 ENG-2433. Migration notes: no consumer-facing API changes; dev container images will be rebuilt during release window.
